pages.text: A correspondence is a bounded answer the world gives to a named question. Spatial, stability, vitality, and resonance are coordinates in attribute space, not directions.$(br2)The same place can have several answers at once. Their order on a page never changes their identity.

pages.title: Layers, not omens
pages.text: A channel combines dimension, biome, height, and salted noise layers. The result is clamped to its declared range.$(br2)The noise is stable for one world, but the secret behind it is never shown. A report is evidence of a measurement, not a seed-reading ritual.

pages.title: Projection is a choice
pages.text: An attribute field is not a vector of motion. First choose a channel with Project Correspondence Channel; only then may a scalar operation, such as Field Gradient, read its spatial change.$(br2)This extra step is a theorem boundary: a gradient has units per block, while the attribute itself has no physical direction.

pages.title: The anchor's report
pages.text: Inscribe Dimensional Survey with the chalk and execute the anchor. Sneak-use the anchor afterward to inspect the last report.$(br2)It records the generation, eighteen planned samples, a 0--15 redstone signal, the dominant channel, and qualitative intensity bands. It never records the seed, secret, raw samples, or hidden layer coefficients.

pages.title: Starter resonance
pages.text: The starter pack adds mathmod:resonance. Plains gently reinforce it; the Deep Dark adds a stronger correspondence; height bends the overworld curve.$(br2)These are teaching data, not universal laws. A datapack may add bounded declarative channels and layers, but never executable sampler code.
